title: Our Heavenly Father Calls
description: Our Heavenly Father Calls in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 686 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Communion with God and Christ”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our heav-enly Fa-ther calls, And Christ in-vites us near; With both my friend-ship shall be sweet, And my com-mu-nion dear.

lines: With both my friendship shall be sweet,
And wise to guide my way.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
